content: 1. Conduct annual screenings for depressive symptoms in all individuals diagnosed with diabetes. For those with a prior history of depression, perform these assessments more frequently. Utilize age-appropriate and validated screening tools to ensure accuracy, and be prepared to conduct further evaluations for individuals who test positive during the screening process. 2. Evaluate for depression when diabetes-related complications are diagnosed or when there are significant changes in the individual's medical status, as these situations may increase the risk of depressive symptoms. 3. Refer individuals exhibiting depressive symptoms to behavioral health professionals or healthcare providers trained in evidence-based treatments for depression. This referral should be integrated into a collaborative care approach that involves the diabetes treatment team to ensure comprehensive management of both conditions.
